reading.body:
CGCN Group filed 67 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI, and its largest AI client is BSA, the Software Alliance, with 14 filings.

The client list is the substance here. BSA, News Corporation, C3.ai, Samsung Semiconductor, Mastercard, Microsoft, and Regions Financial span software trade association, media, enterprise AI, chip manufacturing, payments, and banking. That is not one industry lobbying on AI. It is a set of sectors that each expect AI rules to touch them, and they have retained the same firm to carry the message. Samsung Semiconductor is the one client whose interests run directly into the physical layer of AI, the chips, which is where compute supply and power demand are decided.

The lobbyist counts show how the work is staffed. Scott Riplinger and John Stipicevic each appear on 67 filings, the full set, while Sam Geduldig appears on 54 and the counts fall from there to Aaron Szabo at 6. A small core carries nearly everything, with a longer bench brought in selectively. The bills named, HR 2385, S 2081, S 2750, HR 633, S 3150, S 1792, S 146, and HR 4142, are all drawn from filings dated 2025 or later, so the legislative targets are current rather than historical.

What the data does not say is what any of these clients argued. A filing reports that a firm lobbied on an issue, not the position taken, so the direction of the advocacy is invisible here. The data also does not show spending, outcomes, or which provisions of the named bills mattered. It establishes who is at the table and how often, and nothing about what they won.

summary: CGCN GROUP, LLC filed 67 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 76992.
